index.title: Spare parts
index.subtitle: Holding a part without knowing its name or how to order it? Start from your engine: you never search for a part by name — you spot it visually on an exploded view. The name and the reference are the result of the search, not its starting point.

steps.identify: Identify the engine: brand, model code and serial number from the identification plate.
steps.assembly: Pick the functional assembly: carburetor, ignition, lower unit…
steps.sheet: Spot the part on the catalog's exploded view and note its reference.
steps.order: Add it to your repair list and order from a dealer.

index.eligibilityHint: Part identification relies on the engines registered on your boats. Add an engine from a boat's page to get started.

common.sourceNote: References and indicative prices observed on dealer catalogs (Partzilla, Boats.net, Crowley Marine) — always double-check on your engine's exploded view before ordering.

identify.title: Identify a part
identify.intro: Everything starts from the engine's exact identity: the same assembly exists in dozens of variants depending on the model code and year.

engineCard.title: Step 1 — Identify the engine
engineCard.missingHint: Fill in the engine's record with the identification plate details: they are required to open the right catalog.

serialWarning.title: The serial number tells variants apart
serialWarning.text: The same model code sometimes spans several decades of production. In the catalog, the serial number is what tells the variants apart: note it from the plate before ordering.
serialWarning.ambiguous: Code "{model}" matches {count} catalogue models: only the serial number tells them apart.

plate.title: Where is the identification plate?
plate.intro: The plate carries the brand, the model code and the serial number. Its location depends on the brand:

yamaha.location: On the clamp bracket (the stirrup that grips the transom), sometimes under the cowling.
yamaha.example: Example: “6E0” is the model code (4/5 hp), “500552” the serial number.

johnson_evinrude.location: On the transom side of the clamp bracket or under the cowling, depending on the year.
johnson_evinrude.example: Example: the code “J50PLEA” decodes as a 1999 Johnson 50 hp — Crowley Marine's decoding tool does the translation.

mercury_mariner.location: On the clamp bracket or on the block, under the cowling; the serial number is the catalog's entry key.

plate.unknownBrand: This engine's brand isn't covered by our plate hints yet: the plate is almost always on the clamp bracket, the transom bracket or the block, under the cowling.

suzuki.location: On the clamp bracket, starboard side, or on the block under the cowling.

honda.location: On the clamp bracket or on the crankcase under the cowling; the plate carries the engine type and serial number.

tohatsu.location: On the clamp bracket; recent models also carry a label under the cowling.

selva.location: On the clamp bracket; the powerheads are Yamaha-built, and the matching Yamaha reference is often stamped on the engine.

volvo_penta.location: On the rocker cover or timing case, and on the drive leg for a saildrive: two separate plates, take down both.
volvo_penta.example: Example: "D1-20" is the engine designation, the seven-digit number that follows identifies the individual unit.

yanmar.location: On the rocker cover or on the block, heat-exchanger side; the serial number is also stamped on the block.

nanni.location: On the rocker cover; the base engine (Kubota, Toyota) carries its own plate as well, useful for engine parts.

beta_marine.location: On the rocker cover or the sound shield; the underlying Kubota block carries its own plate.

mercruiser.location: On the timing cover or the manifold, and on the drive for a sterndrive: take down both numbers.

assemblies.title: Step 2 — Pick the functional assembly
assemblies.intro: Browse by assembly, not by part name: each assembly matches an exploded view in the catalog, with its official English heading.

assembly.explodedIntro: Exploded views belong to the dealers' catalogs: open your brand's catalog, enter the model code and look for the “{catalogLabel}” assembly. Parts carry a clickable callout number that reveals the official name and the reference.
assembly.modelCodeMissing: First fill in the model code on the engine's record.

decode.title: Decoding a Yamaha reference
decode.text: A Yamaha reference like “{example}” reads as three blocks: the first is the model code, the 5 middle digits ({code}) identify the part's function regardless of the engine, the last one the variant.
decode.searchHint: Type the full reference as-is into a search engine: it surfaces every seller and the aftermarket equivalents.

assembly.partsIntro: French name and English catalog name side by side: the English one is what you will find on the exploded view.

unreferenced.title: Step 4 — Parts without a manufacturer reference
unreferenced.intro: These parts are not ordered by reference: no point searching for a number that doesn't exist. They are bought by dimension or by equivalence.

fuel_hose.label: Fuel hose
fuel_hose.advice: Bought by dimension (inner diameter), black automotive hose only — never clear hose, which hardens and leaks.

clamps_orings.label: Clamps, O-rings, stainless fasteners
clamps_orings.advice: Standard hardware: note the diameter and thread, buy A4 stainless for the marine environment.

spark_plug.label: Spark plug
spark_plug.advice: Bought by NGK or Champion equivalence (the reference is etched on the fitted plug), not by manufacturer reference.

shear_pin.label: Shear pin
shear_pin.advice: Note the diameter and length of the fitted pin; always keep a spare one aboard.

consumables.label: Consumables
consumables.advice: Carburetor cleaner, penetrating oil, marine grease: generic products from the chandlery or automotive aisle.

cart.title: Repair list
cart.intro: Identified parts pile up here; note the reference from the exploded view, then export the list to order.
cart.empty: No part in the list for this engine.

crossLinks.fromDiagnostic: Identify the parts of this assembly: {label}

tabCta.title: Don't know a part's name?
tabCta.text: Start from the engine's model code and spot the part on the catalog's exploded view: the guided path takes you all the way to an orderable reference.

carburetor.label: Carburetor
carburetor.description: Float chamber, jets, needle valve, float: the most frequently disassembled unit on an outboard — most fuel-delivery failures are solved here.

repair_kit.label: Carburetor repair kit
repair_kit.detail: Bundles genuine gaskets, needle valve and jets: usually cheaper than individual parts for a full rebuild.

float_chamber_gasket.label: Float chamber gasket
float_chamber_gasket.kit: Included in the carburetor repair kit — usually a better deal than the part alone.

needle_valve.label: Needle valve
needle_valve.kit: Included in the carburetor repair kit — usually a better deal than the part alone.

main_jet.label: Main jet
main_jet.detail: The size is etched on it: replace like for like, never ream out a clogged jet.

float.label: Float
float.detail: A fuel-soaked cork float floods the chamber: replace it with the current plastic model.

fuel_system.label: Fuel tank and fuel system
fuel_system.description: From tank to carburetor: tank, primer bulb, hoses, filter and fuel pump.

fuel_pump_kit.label: Fuel pump diaphragm kit
fuel_pump_kit.detail: Diaphragms and check valves of the mechanical pump: a porous diaphragm is a classic fuel-delivery failure.

fuel_pump_diaphragm.label: Fuel pump diaphragm
fuel_pump_diaphragm.kit: Included in the fuel pump kit — usually a better deal than the part alone.

primer_bulb.label: Primer bulb
primer_bulb.detail: A bulb that never firms up when pumping points to an air leak or a tired check valve.

ignition.label: Ignition and electrical
ignition.description: Coils, sensors and the CDI unit: everything that produces and distributes the spark.

cdi_unit.label: CDI unit
cdi_unit.detail: An expensive part that can't be resold untested: rule out coils and the stop switch before blaming it.

stop_switch.label: Stop switch
stop_switch.detail: A shorted stop switch kills all spark: it's the first check, and the cheapest.

power_unit.label: Power unit
power_unit.description: Cylinder head, pistons, rings and gaskets: the block's internal parts.

head_gasket.label: Cylinder head gasket
head_gasket.detail: Replace it every time the head comes off — a reused gasket leaks.

gasket_kit.label: Power head gasket kit
gasket_kit.detail: Every block gasket in one kit: the right call whenever the engine opens up.

anode.label: Internal anode
anode.detail: Sacrificial anode of the cooling circuit: check it at every winterizing.

recoil_starter.label: Recoil starter
recoil_starter.description: Rope, spiral spring and pawls of the pull starter.

starter_rope.label: Starter rope
starter_rope.detail: Also sold by the meter, by dimension; replace it at the first cut strand, before it snaps at sea.

lower_unit.label: Lower unit and water pump
lower_unit.description: Gear housing, water pump, shaft seals: the submerged part of the engine.

impeller.label: Water pump impeller
impeller.detail: The number-one wear part: replace it every 2 seasons or as soon as the tell-tale weakens.

water_pump_kit.label: Water pump kit
water_pump_kit.detail: Impeller, housing, gaskets and key: prefer the full kit over the impeller alone if the pump housing is scored.

drain_screw_gasket.label: Drain screw gasket
drain_screw_gasket.detail: Replace it at every gearcase oil change: it's what keeps the water out.

propeller.label: Propeller
propeller.detail: Diameter and pitch are etched on the hub; a slipping rubber hub (spun hub) can't be seen with the naked eye.

cowling.label: Cowling
cowling.description: Top cowling, bottom cowling, latches and seals.

cowling_seal.label: Cowling seal
cowling_seal.detail: A tired cowling seal lets spray onto the ignition.

bracket.label: Clamp bracket, tilt
bracket.description: Transom clamp bracket, tilt pins and external anodes.

anode.label: Bracket anode
anode.detail: External sacrificial anode: replace it once half eaten away.

cooling_raw_water.label: Raw water circuit
cooling_raw_water.description: Raw water pump, impeller, heat exchanger and anodes: the circuit that cools the engine with the water you sail in.

impeller.label: Raw water pump impeller
impeller.detail: The number-one wear part: replace it every season, and keep a spare on board.

pump_repair_kit.label: Water pump repair kit
pump_repair_kit.detail: Impeller, seals, cover plate and bearings: prefer it over the impeller alone if the pump housing is scored.

pump_cover_gasket.label: Pump cover gasket
pump_cover_gasket.kit: Included in the water pump repair kit.

heat_exchanger_anode.label: Heat exchanger pencil anode
heat_exchanger_anode.detail: Sacrificial anode screwed into the heat exchanger: check it at every winterizing, it protects the whole circuit.

heat_exchanger_gasket_kit.label: Heat exchanger gasket kit
heat_exchanger_gasket_kit.detail: Tube stack seals and O-rings, to be replaced when the exchanger comes apart for descaling.

strainer_seal.label: Strainer cover seal
strainer_seal.detail: The raw water strainer seal: an air leak here and the pump loses its prime.

cooling_fresh_water.label: Fresh water cooling
cooling_fresh_water.description: Thermostat, hoses, expansion tank: the closed coolant loop of a heat-exchanged engine.

thermostat.label: Thermostat
thermostat.detail: An engine that warms up slowly, or overheats for no reason, often starts here.

coolant_hose.label: Coolant hose
coolant_hose.detail: Note the inner diameter and length before ordering: many are sold by the metre.

expansion_tank_cap.label: Expansion tank pressure cap
expansion_tank_cap.detail: A cap that no longer holds pressure will boil an otherwise healthy circuit.

injection.label: Fuel and injection
injection.description: Water-separating pre-filter, filters, injectors: on a diesel, clean fuel is the first cause of trouble.

pre_filter_element.label: Water-separating pre-filter element
pre_filter_element.detail: The Racor and its equivalents: change the element every season, drain the bowl as soon as water shows.

fuel_filter.label: Engine fuel filter
fuel_filter.detail: The second filter, on the engine itself: change it together with the pre-filter.

injector.label: Injector
injector.detail: Tested and calibrated on a bench by a diesel shop: a dribbling injector blackens the exhaust.

injector_seal_kit.label: Injector seal kit
injector_seal_kit.kit: Copper washers and heat shields, always replaced when an injector comes out.

exhaust.label: Wet exhaust
exhaust.description: Exhaust elbow, water lock, hose: the line where raw water joins the gases — and where corrosion works.

exhaust_elbow.label: Exhaust elbow
exhaust_elbow.detail: A wear part: it scales up and corrodes from the inside. Remove and inspect it every 4 to 5 years.

elbow_gasket.label: Exhaust elbow gasket
elbow_gasket.kit: Always replaced when the elbow comes off.

waterlock.label: Water lock
waterlock.detail: Keeps water from siphoning back into the engine at rest: a cracked water lock is replaced, not repaired.

exhaust_hose.label: Exhaust hose
exhaust_hose.detail: Purpose-made wire-reinforced marine hose: an ordinary water hose collapses and burns.

hose_clamps.label: Stainless hose clamps
hose_clamps.detail: Always in pairs on an exhaust joint, screws offset so both stay reachable.

gearbox.label: Marine gear and coupling
gearbox.description: Gearbox, oil, shift cable and flexible coupling: what passes the power to the propeller — or stops passing it.

gear_oil.label: Gearbox oil
gear_oil.detail: ATF or engine oil depending on the model: check the manual, one does not stand in for the other.

output_seal.label: Output shaft oil seal
output_seal.detail: An oil trace on the coupling almost always comes from here.

flexible_coupling.label: Flexible coupling
flexible_coupling.detail: Absorbs vibration between gearbox and shaft: a cracked rubber shows at a glance.

damper_plate.label: Damper plate
damper_plate.detail: Between flywheel and gearbox: a rattle at idle in neutral points straight at it.

saildrive.label: Sail drive
saildrive.description: Diaphragm, anodes and gear oil: a sailboat's through-hull drive leg, and the most critical service deadline on board.

diaphragm.label: Rubber diaphragm
diaphragm.detail: This is what keeps the sea out of the boat: mandatory replacement every 7 years, boat ashore.

anode.label: Sail drive anode
anode.detail: Check it at every haul-out: a spent anode leaves the aluminium leg on the front line.

oil_seal.label: Propeller shaft oil seal
oil_seal.detail: Milky gear oil is its calling card: water has found its way in.

sterndrive.label: Stern drive
sterndrive.description: Bellows, universal joints, trim cylinders and anodes: the drive leg of a sterndrive installation.

bellows_kit.label: Bellows kit
bellows_kit.detail: Drive, exhaust and shift bellows: they are replaced together, every 4 to 5 years.

u_joint.label: Universal joint
u_joint.detail: A squeal when manoeuvring, or grease inside the bellows, points at it.

anode_kit.label: Drive anode kit
anode_kit.detail: Plate, cylinder and propeller anodes: check them at every haul-out.

gimbal_bearing.label: Gimbal bearing
gimbal_bearing.detail: Replaced with the bellows off: worth doing in the same yard visit.

shaft_line.label: Shaft line
shaft_line.description: Stuffing box, packing, cutless bearing and shaft: the hull passage of a conventional inboard.

stuffing_box_packing.label: Stuffing box packing
stuffing_box_packing.detail: Sold by the metre in your shaft's section: three turns cut at an angle, cuts staggered.

stuffing_box.label: Stuffing box
stuffing_box.detail: Traditional packing or maintenance-free dripless: both are replaced with the boat ashore.

cutless_bearing.label: Cutless bearing
cutless_bearing.detail: The rubber-and-brass stern tube bearing: play felt by hand on the shaft means it is done.

shaft_anode.label: Shaft anode
shaft_anode.detail: A sacrificial collar clamped on the shaft: replace it at every haul-out.

starting_charging.label: Starting and charging
starting_charging.description: Starter, alternator, belt and solenoid: the circuit that cranks the engine and charges the batteries.

starter_motor.label: Starter motor
starter_motor.detail: A single click with no cranking is more often the solenoid or the terminals than the starter itself.

drive_belt.label: Alternator drive belt
drive_belt.detail: Black dust under the pulley or a charge that plateaus: always start with the belt and its tension.

lubrication.label: Lubrication
lubrication.description: Oil filter, pump and sump gaskets: the oil change and everything that goes with it.

oil_filter.label: Oil filter
oil_filter.detail: Change it at every oil change: the filter costs less than the oil it protects.

engine_oil.label: Engine oil
engine_oil.detail: Grade and specification per the engine manual: an automotive oil does not suit every marine engine.

air_intake.label: Air intake and turbo
air_intake.description: Air filter, turbo, intercooler: what feeds a diesel's combustion, turbocharged or not.

air_filter.label: Air filter element
air_filter.detail: Often a washable foam element on small marine diesels: clean it rather than bin it.

turbocharger.label: Turbocharger
turbocharger.detail: A new whistle or blue smoke under acceleration: a reconditioned exchange unit often costs far less than new.

breather_filter.label: Crankcase breather filter
breather_filter.detail: A blocked breather pressurises the crankcase and makes the seals weep.

controls.label: Controls and steering
controls.description: Control box, cables, steering: what links the helm to the engine, whatever the motorisation.

throttle_cable.label: Throttle cable
throttle_cable.detail: Ordered at an exact length (in feet from US builders): measure the old one first.

steering_seal_kit.label: Hydraulic steering seal kit
steering_seal_kit.detail: Spongy or weeping steering at the helm: the seal kit costs ten times less than the cylinder.

reference.label: Manufacturer reference
reference.unverified: Not re-checked — confirm it on the exploded view before ordering.
